title: Russian Republic
capsule: The Russian Republic was the short-lived democratic state proclaimed on 1 September 1917 after the Provisional Government under Alexander Kerensky abolished the monarchy following Nicholas II's abdication. It governed a country in deepening crisis — military collapse, peasant unrest, and competing Soviet councils — for barely two months. On 25 October 1917 (O.S.), the Bolshevik Revolution overthrew the Provisional Government, and the All-Russian Congress of Soviets transferred power to the Council of People's Commissars, extinguishing the republic before a constituent assembly could meet.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is taken as coterminous with the late Russian Empire; the republic never established new administrative boundaries, so the geometry is inherited from tsarist administrative records and is well-documented but technically represents the empire's footprint rather than any distinct republican delimitation.
